Undergraduate Research Grants fund academic and creative projects, designed and executed under faculty supervision. Students of all years and majors are eligible.
Academic-year grants provide up to $1,000 and summer grants offer a stipend of $3,000.  Additional funds for international research travel are available.
Students who will present research findings or creative productions may apply for conference travel grants (max. $500).
See the web site for guidelines, project requirements, deadlines, and the online application. Consult a faculty member to develop your ideas into a proposal.

For questions about the grants and advice on writing your proposal, come and learn more every Wednesday at 4 pm, 1940 Sheridan Road (Office of Fellowships). Individual appointments can also be arranged.
urg@northwestern.edu or (847) 467-0499, or for more information, online at www.northwestern.edu/undergrad-research.

We are pleased to present the fourth annual edition of the Northwestern Undergraduate Research Journal.  Through these past years, NURJ has been part of a Northwestern effort to involve and recognize distinguished undergraduates in current, state-of-the-art research.  Our journal provides a medium for undergraduates to share their exceptional work with the entire Northwestern community.

With this issue, we gladly announce that we have opened NURJ to publication in the humanities and social sciences, in addition to the natural sciences and engineering.  This is an ongoing endeavor to integrate all areas of this campus and showcase the diverse research experiences of all participating undergraduates.  Two authors in this issue, Allison Moy from Communication Sciences and Disorders and Nicholas Anderman from English, present exemplary work from the newest fields to be included in NURJ.  We are proud that they have taken this opportunity.

Opportunities are numerous for students at Northwestern, and inspiration comes from all angles and directions.  We hope that NURJ is one among many other inspirations.  We further aim for NURJ to maintain an open relationship with you, the readers, so that we can further display the breadth of remarkable undergraduate research performed at Northwestern.  Therefore, we invite you to offer us your thoughts on the current state and future of NURJ.
